s99502c3ca2.why: Recovering the unreleased encoder lets teams train new voices on matching labels, though the paper flags pitfalls in verification.

s2fa93f2178.title: DAiSy: Online Data Selection by Adaptive Utility Estimation for LLM Pretraining
s2fa93f2178.description: arXiv:2611.32294v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Model-aware online data selection prioritizes the training documents that contribute the most given the model's current state. Existing online selectors rank candidates upon gradient-based data utility scores, which requires the full forward-backward pass of the main model on every candidate document. Scoring each document therefore pays as much as training on it, yet only a small fraction is used for the real model update. We introduce DAiSy, a lightweight linear auxiliary model that learns to predict data utility scores from frozen document embeddings, which eliminates the computation overhead and infrastructure burdens. The linear estimator is updated alongside the main language model, fitting to the exact gradient-based utility scores o
s2fa93f2178.summary: Researchers introduce DAiSy, a lightweight linear auxiliary model that predicts data utility scores from frozen document embeddings for online LLM pretraining data selection.
s2fa93f2178.why: It avoids a full forward-backward pass per candidate document, which could cut the cost of online data selection during pretraining.

sd0f7225165.title: Query-Guided Visual Minimization for Selective Disclosure to Cloud VLMs
sd0f7225165.description: arXiv:2611.32302v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Cloud-hosted vision-language models (VLMs) require sending images beyond the user's local trust boundary, potentially exposing sensitive information the query does not need. We study query-guided visual minimization: a trusted local transformation preserves query-relevant visual content and reduces unnecessary disclosure before transmission. Unlike query-agnostic anonymization, it preserves the same sensitive content when the query requires it and suppresses it otherwise. We introduce QGVM, a framework that combines query grounding with an independent sensitive-item inventory, determines disclosure necessity at the type, instance, and text-content levels, and renders a minimized image for a black-box downstream VLM. We evaluate QGVM on comp
sd0f7225165.summary: Researchers propose QGVM, a framework that locally minimizes images to disclose only query-relevant visual content before sending them to cloud vision-language models.
sd0f7225165.why: Teams sending images to cloud VLMs can reduce exposure of sensitive content the query does not need.

s4f8a4b9b16.title: ASTERISM: Do Multimodal LLMs Actually Look at All the Images?
s4f8a4b9b16.description: arXiv:2611.32316v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Multi-image benchmarks aim to test whether a multimodal large language model (MLLM) combines evidence across images, but many of their items can be answered from a single image. Across about 33k items from 19 public benchmarks, our audit and a two-stage single-image filter find that one image or the question alone settles 24.2% of them. On these items, MLLMs recover from one image a median 78% of the accuracy that all images add over the text alone, so these items reward answering from one image, which we call the single-image shortcut. MLLMs take this shortcut even on items where one image is not enough. On such items, most of their wrong answers repeat an answer they give from one image, at a rate well above chance. We build ASTERISM, to
s4f8a4b9b16.summary: An audit of about 33k items from 19 multi-image benchmarks finds that 24.2% can be answered from a single image or the question alone, a shortcut MLLMs exploit.
s4f8a4b9b16.why: Benchmark scores may overstate multi-image reasoning, so teams should check whether evaluations actually require combining images.

s1996ce42d6.title: SPRUNN: Structural Proximity for Pruning in Deep Neural Networks
s1996ce42d6.description: arXiv:2611.32317v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Deep Neural Networks (DNNs) have demonstrated significant accuracy across various machine learning tasks. However, these networks suffer from a huge number of parameters and computations, which leads to time-consuming processes. Consequently, parameter pruning approaches have been proposed to compress DNNs and efficiently implement them. The main challenge in pruning is selecting the appropriate parameters for pruning without significantly damaging the accuracy. In this paper, we propose SPRUNN, an algorithmic pruning approach based on the structural proximity criterion for filter pruning in convolutional layers of deep neural networks. Structural Proximity (SP) calculates filter similarity by considering all filters and comparing each one
s1996ce42d6.summary: Researchers propose SPRUNN, a structural-proximity-based pruning approach for deep neural networks that aims to reduce parameters without large accuracy loss.
s1996ce42d6.why: Pruning that preserves accuracy could make deploying compressed DNNs faster and cheaper.

s69886e8810.title: When Exact Token Importance Is Not Enough: Limits of Top-K Selection in LLM Attention
s69886e8810.description: arXiv:2611.32324v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Long-context language models often retain only a limited set of past token positions for an attention query. A common strategy scores positions individually and keeps the highest-ranked K. Yet attention weights are renormalized over the chosen set: two individually important positions need not form the best pair. We ask whether independent ranking suffices even when each importance score measures the exact downstream change in next-token predictions caused by deleting that position alone. It does not. A four-position construction makes the ranked pair incur 133.2 times the Kullback-Leibler (KL) divergence of the optimal pair, and a parametric family proves that this multiplicative gap is unbounded. An exact exchange identity and preference
s69886e8810.summary: A paper shows that ranking token positions independently by exact importance and keeping the top K can fail in LLM attention, because attention weights renormalize over the chosen set.
s69886e8810.why: Top-K KV cache selection heuristics may pick suboptimal token sets, which matters for long-context inference design.

s3e21e7f1c7.title: A recursive self-improvement framework for electron microscopy analysis
s3e21e7f1c7.description: arXiv:2611.32325v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Resolving local atomic structures such as defects and interfaces from electron microscopy contrast relies heavily on researcher judgement, leading to low efficiency and subjective standards. Here we present PhyEvo-Mic-RSI, a physics-guided and expert-informed recursive self-improvement framework that turns one-off human corrections into reusable, verifiable capabilities by updating executable operators, parameters and routing rules with versioned inheritance. Given researcher-defined tasks, the system selects analysis paths from image features without expert labels, while testing and inheriting code updates under fixed budgets. Combining physical priors with expert feedback improves atomic point-defect detection over larger models and raise
s3e21e7f1c7.summary: Researchers present PhyEvo-Mic-RSI, a physics-guided recursive self-improvement framework that turns expert corrections into reusable, versioned analysis operators for electron microscopy.
s3e21e7f1c7.why: It shows a method for capturing one-off expert corrections as reusable, verifiable pipeline components in scientific analysis.

s92e4c99e9f.title: Part-Set Prototypes for Explainable Mountain Gazelles Sex Classification
s92e4c99e9f.description: arXiv:2611.32343v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Self-explainable visual models for fine-grained recognition are often hindered by rigid geometric constraints that cannot capture diverse semantic shapes in unconstrained "in-the-wild" imagery. Real-world camera-trap data introduces challenges, including non-optimal poses, lighting variations, occlusions, animal camouflage, and environmental shortcuts. To address this, we introduce set prototypes, a general architecture where both part cardinality and unconstrained spatial layouts are mined directly from data. Our joint-matching formulation places parts simultaneously on a frozen DINOv3 token grid via truncated Sinkhorn competition, allowing unsupported parts to abstain without spatial collapse. We evaluate our approach on Mountain Gazelle
s92e4c99e9f.summary: Researchers introduce set prototypes for self-explainable visual classification of mountain gazelle sex from camera-trap images.
s92e4c99e9f.why: The text gives little on broader engineering implications beyond this specific wildlife classification application.

s1bdfcb7f36.title: DiCT: Teaching X-ray Vision-Language Models to Reason via Imagining CT
s1bdfcb7f36.description: arXiv:2611.32344v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Diagnosing with X-rays often requires reasoning about the 3D locations of abnormalities and their spatial relationships to surrounding anatomical structures, yet such reasoning remains challenging due to the loss of spatial information in 2D projections. To address this challenge, we propose Dreaming in CT (DiCT), a three-stage progressive CT-to-X-ray reasoning transfer framework that leverages a CT vision-language model (VLM) to guide an X-ray VLM. Through this CT-guided transfer, the student acquires CT-informed 3D reasoning capabilities, enabling it to reason directly from 2D X-rays without explicit CT reconstruction at inference time. The framework begins with instruct the dreamer, which equips the X-ray student with initial CT-oriented
s1bdfcb7f36.summary: Researchers propose DiCT, a three-stage framework where a CT vision-language model guides an X-ray VLM to acquire CT-informed 3D reasoning for diagnosis.

s56549f038d.title: Validating Multi-Model AI-Generated Acceptance Criteria in Requirements Engineering
s56549f038d.description: arXiv:2611.32374v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly used in software engineering to generate artifacts such as requirements, user stories, acceptance criteria, documentation, and code. Their use in requirements engineering raises important questions about correctness, traceability, and hallucination, especially because flawed specifications can affect later design, implementation, and verification activities. While much recent work on AI-assisted software engineering has focused on code generation and code-level validation, the validation of AI-generated specifications has received less attention. This paper addresses this gap by presenting a validation-oriented approach for AI-generated acceptance criteria. The approach combines retrieval-augmen
s56549f038d.summary: A paper studies validating AI-generated acceptance criteria in requirements engineering, focusing on correctness, traceability, and hallucination in LLM-generated specifications.
s56549f038d.why: Flawed AI-generated requirements can propagate into design, implementation, and verification, so validation of these artifacts matters.

s428263e91c.title: Does Research-Paper Context Improve LLM-Generated Quadruped Navigation? An Exploratory Simulation Study
s428263e91c.description: arXiv:2611.32381v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Large language models can write competent robot navigation code, but not only does the research on the topic advance, a model may also, due to the volume of findings, fail to recall relevant findings and apply them to the task at hand. In this work, we test whether providing particular research papers as context improves the LLM-written navigation code for the Go2 quadruped, with the LLM (Claude Opus 5) and locomotion policy frozen. Specifically, we compare the navigation controllers the LLM writes when provided with and without particular papers across three settings: behavior trees, navigators edited from a shared base, and controllers written from scratch. When a maze's shortest route is blocked mid-episode, 2 of 8 controllers written wi
s428263e91c.summary: Researchers test whether giving an LLM relevant research papers as context improves the navigation code it writes for a Go2 quadruped robot in simulation.
s428263e91c.why: It suggests retrieving domain research may improve LLM-generated robot control code, though the abstract alone gives limited evidence of the results.

sfdbf0586a2.title: Evolve to Learn: Gradient-aligned experience evolution for model self-improvement
sfdbf0586a2.description: arXiv:2611.32390v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Self-evolving language models can continuously acquire useful experience through test-time interaction, reflection, and prompt optimization, yet turning such experience into model itself to ensure self improvement remains challenging. On-policy self-distillation (OPSD) provides a natural mechanism for internalizing test-time information into model parameters, yet it largely assumes that the gener- ated experience is worth learning. We show that this assumption does not always hold: experiences that improve test-time performance may provide limited or even harmful training signals. To better characterize which experience should be inter- nalized, we systematically analyze diverse mutated experiences across multiple tasks and reflection model
sfdbf0586a2.summary: Researchers propose gradient-aligned experience evolution, arguing that on-policy self-distillation should only internalize experiences that are actually worth learning for model self-improvement.
sfdbf0586a2.why: Experiences that improve test-time performance may not be worth training into weights, so teams building self-improving models need filtering.

sa97a49c04e.title: Not All Pairs Align: Caption-Guided Audio-Visual Contrastive Learning
sa97a49c04e.description: arXiv:2611.32399v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We address the problem of learning audio-visual representations from co-occurring modalities. Multimodal contrastive learning typically assumes that paired observations provide shared views of the same underlying information. While this may be true for datasets collected in constrained environments, it does not always hold. For instance, co-occurring audio and visual signals can differ substantially in their content due to off-screen sounds. Nevertheless, standard contrastive objectives treat all paired samples as equally aligned. In this work, we propose Caption Guided Alignment Aware Loss (CGAAL), a model-agnostic objective that leverages modality-specific captions to estimate semantic agreement between audio and video. CGAAL uses these a
sa97a49c04e.summary: Researchers propose caption-guided audio-visual contrastive learning, arguing standard objectives wrongly treat all audio-visual pairs as equally aligned despite off-screen sounds.
sa97a49c04e.why: Standard multimodal contrastive training may learn from misaligned pairs, so pair-quality handling could matter for multimodal representation training.

sbd84689e4b.title: Verify then Steer: Progress Hallucination-Aware Recovery for Continuous Vision-and-Language Navigation
sbd84689e4b.description: arXiv:2611.32400v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Vision-and-Language Navigation (VLN) requires an agent to follow language instructions to reach a target in an unseen 3D environment. However, existing methods still struggle to recover from route deviations at test time. We investigate this limitation through the lens of instruction progress, and trace it to a phenomenon we term progress hallucination: agents misinterpret off-route observations as evidence of task progress, causing their internal instruction progress to advance beyond the actual task stage and hindering recovery based on earlier sub-instructions. To address this failure mode, we propose PHAR (Progress Hallucination-Aware Recovery), a test-time recovery framework following a verify-then-steer paradigm. The verifier examines
sbd84689e4b.summary: Researchers identify progress hallucination in vision-and-language navigation, where agents mistake off-route observations for task progress, and propose a verify-then-steer recovery method.
sbd84689e4b.why: Agents that misjudge task progress after route deviations can fail to recover, a reliability issue for embodied AI deployments.

s3152e3ca49.title: CPU-Eval: Evaluating Large Language Models for CPU Hardware Code Generation
s3152e3ca49.description: arXiv:2611.32405v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Benchmarks such as VerilogEval have supported rapid advances in hardware description language (HDL) generation by large language models (LLMs). However, recent HDL-generation systems achieve pass rates above 90% on VerilogEval, leaving limited headroom for revealing further advances. To provide a challenging target for further progress on a practically important hardware-development task, we introduce CPU-Eval, a benchmark of 339 HDL-generation problems constructed from six CPUs. Drawn from practical CPU designs, including families fabricated in silicon, the problems span CPUs from small embedded cores to Linux-capable out-of-order cores and cover diverse CPU functions written in SystemVerilog, Chisel, and SpinalHDL. In each problem, an LLM
s3152e3ca49.summary: Researchers introduce CPU-Eval, a benchmark of 339 hardware description language generation problems drawn from six CPU designs, to test LLMs beyond saturated VerilogEval.
s3152e3ca49.why: Hardware code generation teams get a harder benchmark, since leading systems already exceed 90% pass rates on VerilogEval.

s6687635029.title: BEACON: Learning Observation-Conditioned Starting Points for Guided Conditional Flow Matching in Microscopy
s6687635029.description: arXiv:2611.32406v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Fluorescence microscopy drives much of modern life science, but accessible imaging setups often yield images degraded by out-of-focus light, limited resolution, and strong signal-dependent noise. Computational restoration can recover high-quality images from such data, enabling cheaper and faster imaging at lower light dose, provided biologically meaningful structures are preserved. Guided conditional flow matching has recently shown strong results for microscopy dehazing and computational super-resolution by learning distributions of plausible restorations. However, it pairs each clean target with an independent standard Gaussian sample, so the starting point of every training path does not leverage the degraded observation. This arbitrary
s6687635029.summary: Researchers present BEACON, which learns observation-conditioned starting points for guided conditional flow matching to restore degraded fluorescence microscopy images.
s6687635029.why: It offers a method for computational microscopy restoration that aims to preserve biologically meaningful structures while enabling lower light dose imaging.

s857c0ca850.title: Within-task hazards of AI agents: unidentified by time-horizon curves, identified by repeated runs
s857c0ca850.description: arXiv:2611.32415v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The time horizon of an AI agent is read off a curve: the probability that the agent completes a task, plotted against the time a human needs for it. Several recent analyses fit survival models to this curve and conclude that agents' hazard of failure declines as a task goes on. The curve cannot support that conclusion. Every log-logistic horizon curve with slope $\beta\le1$ is a mixture of constant-hazard curves, and in a proportional-hazards frailty model the same curve is produced by every within-task Weibull shape $k\ge\beta$. If runs of a task are conditionally independent, repeated runs restore identification within this model: the probability that two runs both succeed is the single-run curve shifted by $1/k$ on the $\log_2$ time axis
s857c0ca850.summary: A paper argues that AI agent time-horizon curves cannot show whether failure hazard declines within a task, and that repeated runs are needed to identify within-task hazards.
s857c0ca850.why: Teams relying on time-horizon curves to judge agent reliability may draw wrong conclusions about failure patterns; repeated-run data is needed.

s46a7e8b4bd.title: NRG-Twins: Pixel-Level Ground Truth for Rigidity Violations in Generated Videos
s46a7e8b4bd.description: arXiv:2611.32431v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Video generators now produce realistic clips of scenes and objects, which makes generated video an attractive source of 3D content. Yet generated video is not 3D consistent: static content slowly deforms or slides, 3D reconstruction degrades, and the errors are too subtle to label by hand. To make generators 3D consistent, or to build rewards and guidance that push them there, we need data that say where and by how much a generated video breaks rigidity, and these data must come from generated video itself. We obtain per-pixel ground-truth labels from real-generated twins: a real clip paired with its re-creation by a keyframe-conditioned video generator. After inserting real keyframes so that the twin camera roughly follows the real one, we
s46a7e8b4bd.summary: Researchers present NRG-Twins, a method providing pixel-level ground-truth labels for rigidity violations in generated videos, to help make video generators more 3D consistent.
s46a7e8b4bd.why: Generated video often deforms static content, and per-pixel labels could support training rewards or guidance for more 3D-consistent generators.

s30ca383440.title: See the Answer, Learn to Embed: Learning Universal Multimodal Embeddings from Hindsight
s30ca383440.description: arXiv:2611.32439v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Universal Multimodal Embedding (UME) models map heterogeneous multimodal inputs into a shared embedding space, where pairwise similarity supports diverse downstream tasks. Recent reasoning-driven UME approaches use intermediate reasoning to generate additional context for embedding, but often incur extra computation at inference. In this paper, we explore the matched candidate (i.e., the paired target) as an alternative source of context, asking whether a model can "see the answer" during training and "learn to embed" without it at inference. However, direct conditioning on this privileged context can introduce candidate-specific information unavailable from the query alone or cause the candidate-conditioned query representation to collapse
s30ca383440.summary: Researchers propose learning universal multimodal embeddings by letting models see the matched candidate during training, avoiding extra inference-time reasoning computation.
s30ca383440.why: Training with hindsight context could yield embedding models that avoid the added inference cost of reasoning-driven approaches.

sb7492e3653.title: Describe, Don't Ask: Caption-Driven On-Policy Distillation for Fine-Grained Visual Perception
sb7492e3653.description: arXiv:2611.32463v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Vision-language models (VLMs) often recognize fine-grained details more accurately in a relevant crop than in the full image. Multimodal on-policy distillation (OPD) methods exploit this by transferring the advantage of a crop-view teacher to a full-image student. However, their supervision relies on region-specific questions curated through an elaborate synthesis pipeline, which brings three weaknesses: (1) every region needs a question--answer pair written exclusively for it, locking training into costly QA curation that is hard to scale to unlabeled images; (2) all rollouts of a region answer the same question, so the teacher supervises only the details it asks about, leaving other visual elements in the region unsupervised; and (3) ever
sb7492e3653.summary: Researchers propose caption-driven on-policy distillation to improve vision-language models' fine-grained perception, reducing reliance on costly region-specific question-answer curation.
sb7492e3653.why: Replacing per-region QA curation with captions could make fine-grained visual distillation easier to scale for multimodal training pipelines.

s845fbc3039.title: Gamification in the age of AI: surveying player perceptions of motivation, manipulation, and data protection
s845fbc3039.description: arXiv:2611.32464v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Modern games and applications increasingly employ artificial intelligence (AI), user modeling, and gamification to influence user behavior, sustain engagement, and monetize attention. Although these mechanisms can enhance motivation and enjoyment, they also raise concerns about manipulation, personal data usage, and transparency. To examine how players perceive these dynamics, we conducted a survey with 28 adult participants. Respondents expressed strong concerns about the collection and exploitation of personal information in games and gamified applications, while also reporting low awareness and a limited sense of control over how their data is used. They evaluated progression features such as leveling systems and leaderboards as motivati
s845fbc3039.summary: A survey of 28 adults finds players are concerned about manipulation, personal data collection, and transparency in AI-driven gamification.
s845fbc3039.why: Small survey of player attitudes; relevant mainly to teams designing engagement features that use user modeling and personal data.

s6a9f9450ad.title: Progressive Reliable Supervision for Black-Box Universal Domain Adaptation
s6a9f9450ad.description: arXiv:2611.32474v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Black-Box Universal Domain Adaptation (B$^2$-UniDA) aims to adapt a target model to an unlabeled target domain under arbitrary label-space relationships, while neither source data nor source-model parameters are accessible during adaptation. Under such restrictive information access, reliable target supervision is unavailable, while predictions from the black-box source model can be unreliable due to source bias and domain shifts. To address this challenge, we propose Progressive Reliable Supervision (PReS), which progressively establishes and refines reliable target supervision by coordinating complementary knowledge from the black-box source model, foundation models, and the evolving target model. PReS first identifies reliable known samp
s6a9f9450ad.summary: Researchers propose Progressive Reliable Supervision (PReS) for black-box universal domain adaptation, where neither source data nor source-model parameters are accessible.
s6a9f9450ad.why: Adapting models without source data or parameters addresses a restrictive deployment setting, though the abstract offers limited detail on results.

s18394dd955.title: CodeWAM: A Code World Action Model for End-to-End Autonomous Driving
s18394dd955.description: arXiv:2611.32483v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Driving world models anticipate action consequences through representations of how the world evolves. For autonomous driving, these representations must capture both the surrounding scene and the ego vehicle's motion under a candidate plan. We propose CodeWAM, a driving world model that incorporates executable code as part of its world representation. Code represents ego dynamics by expressing how the vehicle state evolves under plan execution, while a learned visual model captures scene-dependent consequences. Executing the code produces a candidate-conditioned motion sequence, which is evaluated relative to the prior plan and recorded motion history. The resulting execution consequences and learned scene outcomes jointly represent the can
s18394dd955.summary: Researchers propose CodeWAM, a driving world model that represents ego vehicle dynamics as executable code alongside a learned visual model for end-to-end autonomous driving.
s18394dd955.why: Combining executable code with learned visual models for driving planning is an architectural idea engineers in autonomy may evaluate.

s32df646f51.title: Assessing Robustness to Catastrophic Forgetting in Continual Deep Reinforcement Learning for Cyber-Physical Systems
s32df646f51.description: arXiv:2611.32496v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: As the use of reinforcement learning (RL) becomes more widespread in cyber-physical systems, it becomes increasingly important to design RL agents that are able to adapt to changes in their environments in order to maintain safety and reliability. This paper addresses the question of whether different classes of RL algorithm are more robust against forgetting previously learned behaviours, a critical issue in continual learning, in non-stationary environments. We evaluate the robustness of representative examples of three important classes of RL algorithm in a non-stationary autonomous parking environment. These are Proximal Policy Optimization (PPO), which is a model-free on-policy algorithm, Soft-Actor-Critic (SAC), which is a model-free
s32df646f51.summary: Researchers evaluate how robust three classes of reinforcement learning algorithms are to catastrophic forgetting in continual learning for cyber-physical systems.
s32df646f51.why: Forgetting previously learned behaviours threatens safety in deployed RL controllers that must adapt to changing environments.

s382df81fd4.title: Branch and Consolidate: A Unified Recipe for Multi-Teacher On-Policy Distillation
s382df81fd4.description: arXiv:2611.32515v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Specialists post-trained from a shared checkpoint acquire complementary capabilities, and multi-teacher on-policy distillation (MOPD) can consolidate them into a single model. However, we find that existing consolidation methods, from weight merging to MOPD, fall short when specialists diverge substantially from the shared checkpoint, whereas prior studies mostly examine specialists that remain close to it. We present a unified recipe for multimodal MOPD that consolidates such specialists back into the single student they branched from. The recipe specifies initialization, data selection, balanced supervision across teachers, and preservation of existing capabilities for consolidation, together with a targeted refinement stage for capabilit
s382df81fd4.summary: Researchers present a unified multimodal multi-teacher on-policy distillation recipe that consolidates specialists which diverge substantially from a shared checkpoint back into one student.
s382df81fd4.why: Existing merging and distillation methods reportedly struggle when specialists drift far from the base checkpoint, relevant to multi-model consolidation work.

s7ea002af9a.title: Wi-Fi Enabled Edge Intelligence Framework for Smart City Traffic Monitoring using Low-Power IoT Cameras
s7ea002af9a.description: arXiv:2611.32517v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Real-time traffic monitoring in smart cities demands ultra-low latency processing to support time-critical decisions such as incident detection and congestion management. While cloud-based solutions offer robust computation, their inherent latency limits their applicability for such tasks. This work proposes a localized edge AI framework that connects low-power IoT camera sensors to a client, or applies offloading of inference to an NVIDIA Jetson Nano (GPU). Networking is achieved via Wi-Fi, enabling image classification without relying on wide-area infrastructure such as 5G, or wired networks. We evaluate two processing strategies: local inference on camera nodes and GPU-accelerated offloading to the Jetson Nano.We show that local processi
s7ea002af9a.summary: Researchers propose a localized edge AI framework connecting low-power IoT cameras to a client or NVIDIA Jetson Nano over Wi-Fi for smart city traffic monitoring.
s7ea002af9a.why: Shows a low-latency edge inference design that avoids cloud round trips for time-critical tasks like incident detection and congestion management.

s67af7e4552.title: ContinualDrive: A Deployment-Anchored, Multi-Axis Benchmark for Continual Updates of Learned Driving Planners
s67af7e4552.description: arXiv:2611.32529v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Learned driving planners keep being updated after deployment as new logs arrive, yet continual learning evaluations rarely ask whether an update improves on the deployed model, and their verdicts rest on unstated evaluation choices. We present ContinualDrive, a deployment-anchored benchmark for post-deployment continual learning of driving planners. It updates a deployed planner on real-world nuPlan logs one scenario-type group at a time, evaluates the same checkpoints in open and closed loop, makes four measurement axes explicit (evaluation loop, reference checkpoint, temporal aggregation and stream protocol), and anchors a three-valued release verdict to the deployed checkpoint. We study two planners (PlanTF and Diffusion Planner) under f
s67af7e4552.summary: ContinualDrive is a benchmark for post-deployment continual updates of learned driving planners, using real nuPlan logs and open and closed loop evaluation.
s67af7e4552.why: Gives teams a way to test whether updating a deployed driving planner actually improves on the current model.

s0e5470d060.title: Next-Manip: On-Demand Agent-Policy Collaboration for Robotic Manipulation
s0e5470d060.description: arXiv:2611.32533v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: General-purpose robotic manipulation requires task reasoning, failure recovery, and precise control, yet limited manipulation data make these abilities difficult to obtain from a single policy. Recent multimodal agents show promise in task reasoning and recovery but lack reliable fine-grained control and incur high inference cost, whereas learned policies provide efficient fine-grained execution but struggle beyond their learned skills. Although their complementary strengths suggest combining the two, doing so requires repeatedly deciding which executor should act as task demands change. Instead of relying on the agent for each decision, we present Next-Manip, an on-demand agent--policy collaboration framework that decouples executor alloca
s0e5470d060.summary: Next-Manip proposes on-demand collaboration between multimodal agents and learned policies for robotic manipulation, switching between them as needed.
s0e5470d060.why: Suggests a hybrid design where expensive reasoning agents are called only when a fast control policy fails.

s52a5367532.title: MXI-MemICL: Towards In-Context Robot Manipulation through Self-Retrieved Interaction Memory
s52a5367532.description: arXiv:2611.32564v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: In-context learning (ICL) offers robots a way to acquire new skills from a single demonstration without parameter updates. However, existing robotic ICL methods either rely on large-scale pretraining constrained by scarce, costly robot interaction data or require additional annotations yet struggle to generalize across tasks. To bridge this gap, we propose MXI-MemICL, a framework for memory-guided ICL in vision-language-action (VLA) models. By treating demonstrations as retrievable memory, MXI-MemICL enables in-context manipulation without additional large-scale pretraining or specialized annotations. Specifically, a visual-action causal encoder turns actions and their observed effects in demonstrations and completed interactions into reusa
s52a5367532.summary: MXI-MemICL introduces memory-guided in-context learning for vision-language-action models, treating robot demonstrations as retrievable memory to learn new manipulation skills.
s52a5367532.why: Offers a way to teach robots new skills from a single demonstration without parameter updates or extra annotations.

s6630e3e4b7.title: Boiling Down Uncertainty: Deep Generative Scenario Search with Decision-Guided Evolution Strategies for Two-Stage Stochastic Optimization
s6630e3e4b7.description: arXiv:2611.32573v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: One of the most common models for handling uncertainty is two-stage stochastic programming. Choosing the right number of scenarios is a trade-off between the uncertainty that can be represented and computational cost. A recent method, Deep Generative Scenario Search, generates synthetic scenarios and improves them by learning from the decisions they induce. The original approach used a black-box gradient estimate, since decisions are piecewise constant across scenarios. This paper provides the missing analytical foundation by deriving the gradient in closed form from recourse duality and an adjoint solve of the regularized reduced problem. The decision-focused direction, with a heuristic direction as a backup when duals are unavailable, def
s6630e3e4b7.summary: Researchers derive analytical gradients for Deep Generative Scenario Search, a method that generates and refines scenarios for two-stage stochastic optimization.
s6630e3e4b7.why: Provides a theoretical foundation for a scenario generation method, which may improve decision quality under uncertainty.

s2812221254.title: Gated Concept Adapters: Layer-Wise Concept Bottlenecks for Auditable Text Understanding
s2812221254.description: arXiv:2611.32600v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Human-facing text understanding systems are used to infer affect, moderate harmful content, and support socially sensitive decisions. However, Transformer predictions are difficult to audit because they are produced from high-dimensional hidden states that do not provide a compact, inspectable interface for human analysis or intervention. We introduce Gated Concept Adapters (GCA), a layer-wise concept bottleneck framework that attaches gated, low-dimensional concept-producing readout adapters to selected outputs of pretrained Transformers. Token representations are mapped into concept activations, filtered by learned gates, pooled into layer-level summaries, and exposed to the prediction head as a concept-mediated interface. The dimensions
s2812221254.summary: Gated Concept Adapters add layer-wise, low-dimensional concept bottlenecks to pretrained Transformers to make text understanding predictions more inspectable and auditable.
s2812221254.why: Offers a route to auditable intervention points in models used for moderation and other sensitive text decisions.

s2d41d08eac.title: RoboRecast: Intent-Preserving Demonstration Augmentation via Diagnosis-Driven Optimization
s2d41d08eac.description: arXiv:2611.32622v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Collecting diverse real-world manipulation demonstrations is costly, motivating the use of simulation to augment existing demonstrations for robot policy learning. When objects, layouts, or robots change, transferring motions from a source demonstration can produce behavior that is semantically implausible or physically infeasible in the new setting. We introduce RoboRecast, an agentic optimization framework that preserves the interactions required by the source task while jointly optimizing the simulated scene and robot motion to make those interactions executable in the target setting. When an interaction fails, the agent uses simulation feedback to diagnose the cause, revise the relevant scene or motion parameters, and test whether the r
s2d41d08eac.summary: RoboRecast is an agentic optimization framework that augments robot demonstrations in simulation by jointly adjusting scene and robot motion while preserving task interactions.
s2d41d08eac.why: Could reduce the cost of collecting real-world manipulation demonstrations for robot policy learning.

s4de2b71113.title: REBEAL: Human References Are No Longer the Best Translation, and Metrics Do Not Notice
s4de2b71113.description: arXiv:2611.32623v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Reference-based MT evaluation assumes the human reference is correct and better than the systems it scores. Both assumptions now fail, since the human reference ranks first in none of the 2024 WMT MQM campaigns and carries annotated errors in 19% to 87% of its segments. What a metric does with a flawed reference is a question about the metric, and it would have been worth asking before reference quality came into doubt. We introduce REBEAL (Reference Bias EvALuation), a benchmark that probes how MT metrics respond to seven types of controlled reference contamination, drawn from the error categories those campaigns record. Across eight widely used metrics and three language pairs, recent learned metrics (xCOMET, MetricX) prove more robust th
s4de2b71113.summary: REBEAL is a benchmark testing how machine translation metrics respond to controlled flaws in human reference translations, noting references contain annotated errors.
s4de2b71113.why: Shows reference-based MT metrics may be unreliable when references are flawed, affecting how teams evaluate translation systems.

s1b397e8a3a.title: MargEmbed-Akan: Bridging Twi Questions and English Knowledge through Cross-Lingual Score Distillation
s1b397e8a3a.description: arXiv:2611.32630v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Most information sought online by Twi (Akan) speakers is written in English, making cross-lingual retrieval essential. We evaluate eight systems: BM25, five open embedding models, and two proprietary models (gemini-embedding-001 and OpenAI text-embedding-3-large) on two Twi-English tasks. AfriQA contains 1,221 natively written Asante Twi questions that must retrieve their answering English Wikipedia passages. Bible translation retrieval requires a Twi passage to retrieve its English translation from 6,195 candidates. We introduce MargEmbed-Akan, a 560M-parameter open query encoder trained from AfriE5-Large-instruct using cross-lingual score distillation. The frozen base model scores each English training question against its answer passage
s1b397e8a3a.summary: The MargEmbed-Akan paper evaluates eight retrieval systems on Twi-English cross-lingual tasks and introduces a distilled embedding model for Twi questions.
s1b397e8a3a.why: Highlights gaps in embedding retrieval for low-resource languages like Twi, relevant to multilingual search builders.

s0270c849bb.title: ReFocus: Progress-Guided Adaptive Practice for Long-Horizon Robotic Manipulation Reinforcement Learning
s0270c849bb.description: arXiv:2611.32639v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Online reinforcement learning (RL) enables vision-language-action policies to improve through environmental interaction. However, in long-horizon manipulation, sparse success/failure feedback provides little information about where policies encounter bottlenecks. Moreover, repeated full-task rollouts also leave these bottlenecks weakly analyzed and insufficiently practiced. To this end, we introduce ReFocus, a progress-guided multi-round RL framework that alternates between Global and Local RL to identify task-specific bottlenecks and allocate additional practice to them. Specifically, during Global RL, we decompose each task into a Directed Acyclic Graph (DAG) of subtasks. Then a DAG-based Progress Reward is leveraged for both policy train
s0270c849bb.summary: ReFocus is a progress-guided multi-round reinforcement learning framework that alternates global and local RL to find and practice bottlenecks in long-horizon robotic manipulation.
s0270c849bb.why: Addresses sparse feedback in long-horizon robot RL by targeting specific bottleneck stages for practice.

s96a046e864.title: BARE: Body-Aware Reflexive Evasion for Humanoid Robots
s96a046e864.description: arXiv:2611.32642v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Dynamic obstacle avoidance is essential for safely deploying humanoid robots in real-world environments, where rapidly approaching objects require immediate evasive responses. Recent advances in reflexive evasion have focused primarily on quadrupeds, which typically rely on large-scale whole-body maneuvers. In contrast, humanoids can exploit their rich body articulation to evade through small, localized body adjustments. By moving threatened body regions without repositioning the entire body, these responses may require less execution time and less surrounding free space. However, local adjustments can alter mass distribution or support conditions, making it challenging to achieve rapid evasion while maintaining whole-body stability. To thi
s96a046e864.summary: BARE proposes body-aware reflexive evasion for humanoid robots, using small localized body adjustments to dodge rapidly approaching obstacles.

s7a419e1772.title: TeamFlowRL: Online Policy Optimization of Decentralized Flow Policies for Multi-Agent Coordination
s7a419e1772.description: arXiv:2611.32645v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Complex cooperative tasks require coordinated multi-agent behavior. Offline generative policies learn expressive cooperative behaviors from trajectories but remain limited by fixed datasets. Online reinforcement learning can improve them through environment interaction. However, fine-tuning flow policies is difficult because action likelihoods are hard to compute. We propose TeamFlowRL, a two-stage framework that pretrains multi-agent flow policies offline and fine-tunes them online. We formulate team policy optimization over the complete denoising trajectories of decentralized flow policies, avoiding intractable action likelihoods. The resulting objective weights each agent's trajectory ratio with a shared team advantage and clips each rat
s7a419e1772.summary: TeamFlowRL pretrains multi-agent flow policies offline and fine-tunes them online with reinforcement learning for cooperative multi-agent coordination.
s7a419e1772.why: Offers a method for improving generative multi-agent policies beyond fixed datasets through online interaction.

s8fd5f0be76.title: ICLWorld: Benchmarking In-Context Learning of Agents from Digital to Physical Worlds
s8fd5f0be76.description: arXiv:2611.32649v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: In-context learning (ICL) lets agents acquire new rules from context and adapt to user-specific requirements at inference time. The same frontier agents now operate both computers and robots, yet their ICL remains insufficiently assessed: existing benchmarks are largely offline, rely on text or static images, and risk training-data contamination, while robot evaluations are limited to method-level ablations. We present ICLWorld, an online benchmark that evaluates the ICL of agents from digital to physical worlds, covering computer use and robot use, together with UIverse, a unified harness that turns every environment into a user interface. We build 30 environments, record 630 demonstration videos (10+ hours), and design 160 tasks with cust
s8fd5f0be76.summary: ICLWorld is an online benchmark that evaluates in-context learning of agents across computer use and robot control in digital and physical settings.
s8fd5f0be76.why: Provides a contamination-resistant way to assess whether agents adapt to new rules at inference time across computers and robots.

s8169ffe3f4.title: DexWAC: A Unified World-Actor-Critic Model for Dexterous Robot Manipulation
s8169ffe3f4.description: arXiv:2611.32654v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Robot demonstrations provide more than actions to imitate: they reveal how actions change the world and how those changes contribute to task success. Recent world-action models (WAMs) extend vision-language-action (VLA) models with the first signal by jointly predicting actions and future observations, yet this predictive ability serves only as an auxiliary loss for policy learning. Meanwhile, most policy improvement methods learn dynamics and values in separate models, increasing training overhead and limiting representation sharing between these complementary objectives. We introduce DexWAC, a unified world-actor-critic model that jointly learns an actor, an action-conditioned world model, and a bootstrapped critic in a single robot pretr
s8169ffe3f4.summary: DexWAC is a unified world-actor-critic model for dexterous robot manipulation that combines action prediction, dynamics, and value learning in one model.
s8169ffe3f4.why: Suggests sharing representations across world modeling and policy learning could reduce training overhead for robot policies.

s02cb518410.title: Bathys: Advancing Deep Search Agents
s02cb518410.description: arXiv:2611.32660v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Deep search is a critical capability for agents tackling complex, open-ended tasks, where solving a problem requires iterative information gathering, query reformulation, and evidence-based verification rather than a single retrieval step. To address these requirements, we present Bathys 9B and 27B deep search agents built around a training framework that spans verifiable question synthesis, post-training, and online reinforcement learning (RL) under context compression. Our high-quality data construction ensures both search depth and reliability: each clue is reformulated as an indirect reference requiring independent retrieval, and retained evidence chains enable verification that the clues jointly determine a unique answer. Curated traje
s02cb518410.summary: Bathys 9B and 27B are deep search agents trained with verifiable question synthesis, post-training, and online RL under context compression.
s02cb518410.why: Describes a training pipeline for multi-step search agents that gather evidence iteratively and verify answers.

sb53d7a1b07.title: Are We Rewarding the Wrong Module? Module-Specific Policy Optimization for Multimodal Reinforcement Learning
sb53d7a1b07.description: arXiv:2611.32687v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards (RLVR) based on Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO) has been widely adopted to enhance the multimodal reasoning of multimodal large language models (MLLMs). However, existing methods share a common limitation of Module-Level Credit Entanglement, in which the vision encoder, projector, and LLM modules are jointly optimized using the same advantage signals even when perceptual correctness and final-answer correctness differ. To address this limitation, we propose Module-Specific Policy Optimization (MSPO), a framework that separates perceptual and outcome-based learning signals across model modules. Specifically, MSPO uses responses to perception checklists comprising auxiliary questions ab
sb53d7a1b07.summary: Researchers propose Module-Specific Policy Optimization to stop RLVR/GRPO from applying one advantage signal to all modules of multimodal LLMs, including the vision encoder, projector, and LLM.
sb53d7a1b07.why: It targets credit-assignment flaws in RL fine-tuning of multimodal models, which could affect how teams train vision-language reasoning systems.

s63f1bdf262.title: FourStat: A Dual AutoEncoder Leveraging Frequency and Stationarity for Time Series Anomaly Detection
s63f1bdf262.description: arXiv:2611.32714v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: While numerous studies have focused on multivariate time series anomaly detection, many existing methods perform poorly or are not directly applicable to univariate settings. We introduce FourStat, a dual-model framework for univariate time series anomaly detection that combines two complementary approaches. The Fourier Autoencoder (FAE) captures global patterns like seasonality through frequency-domain analysis, while the Stationary Autoencoder (SAE) focuses on local structures by enforcing statistical stationarity. We also propose a new evaluation metric called Perfect Point that assesses whether perfect F1-scores can be achieved directly from anomaly scores, eliminating thresholding subjectivity. Results demonstrate that FourStat outperf
s63f1bdf262.summary: FourStat is a dual autoencoder for univariate time series anomaly detection, combining a Fourier autoencoder for global patterns with a stationary autoencoder for local structure.
s63f1bdf262.why: Univariate anomaly detection is a common monitoring need, and the approach claims to address settings where many existing methods perform poorly.

sb20bdd4ba7.title: ASCENT: A Benchmark for Evaluating and Advancing Stepwise Diagnostic Reasoning in Large Language Models on Common Clinical Scenarios
sb20bdd4ba7.description: arXiv:2611.32734v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Large language models (LLMs) excel at medical question answering yet are rarely evaluated on the stepwise diagnostic reasoning that defines real clinical workflows, where impressions are revised as information accumulates. We build Annotated Stepwise Clinical rEasoning for NaturalisTic Diagnosis (ASCENT), a clinician-annotated benchmark and training resource of 3,078 stepwise problems derived from MedQA-USMLE that decomposes each vignette into EMR-aligned steps (Findings, Impression, supporting Rationale), enabling evaluation of intermediate reasoning under incomplete information. Experiments and training with ASCENT revealed insights into how current LLMs handle stepwise diagnostic reasoning. Even strong reasoning models that perform well
sb20bdd4ba7.summary: ASCENT is a clinician-annotated benchmark of 3,078 stepwise diagnostic problems derived from MedQA-USMLE, designed to evaluate how LLMs revise impressions as clinical information accumulates.
sb20bdd4ba7.why: It offers a way to test LLMs on multi-step clinical reasoning rather than only final answers, relevant to healthcare AI evaluation.

s87f93a554c.title: ReQOR: Operator-Discrepancy Subspace Repair for Quantization-Conditioned Backdoors in Large Language Models
s87f93a554c.description: arXiv:2611.32755v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Quantization-Conditioned Backdoors (QCBs) cause large language models (LLMs) to exhibit malicious behavior after quantization while remaining benign at high precision. Existing defenses often rely on security-guided configuration selection or iterative optimization, but do not identify which quantization-induced changes should be repaired. We isolate module-local quantization effects from upstream drift by evaluating the high-precision and quantized versions of each module on identical states from the quantized inference trajectory, and formulate QCB defense as repairing the resulting same-state operator discrepancies. We propose ReQOR, a training-free defense that identifies the dominant directions of these discrepancies on benign calibrat
s87f93a554c.summary: ReQOR proposes a method to repair quantization-conditioned backdoors in LLMs, which behave maliciously only after quantization while appearing benign at high precision.
s87f93a554c.why: Teams that quantize models for deployment may need to verify quantized versions, since backdoors can appear only after compression.

s7a49aba546.title: SGD with Large Learning Rates: General Analysis & Improved Rates
s7a49aba546.description: arXiv:2611.32762v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Stochastic Gradient Descent lies at the core of modern machine learning. However its classical analysis typically restricts the stepsize to be below a curvature-dependent stability threshold. Recent developments in deterministic optimization have challenged this paradigm, showing that suitably chosen large stepsizes can not only preserve convergence, but also accelerate Gradient Descent (GD). Whether this phenomenon persists in the presence of stochastic gradient noise has remained an open question (Wu et al., 2024). In this work, we answer this question affirmatively for the cross-entropy loss with linear predictors and two-layer neural networks, establishing an accelerated $\mathcal{O}(T^{-2})$ convergence rate. At the core of our analysi
s7a49aba546.summary: Researchers analyze stochastic gradient descent with large learning rates and report improved convergence rates, answering an open question about whether large-stepsize benefits persist under gradient noise.
s7a49aba546.why: Results on stepsize choice under noise could inform optimizer tuning, though the text gives limited practical detail.

s263fdd8600.title: C3H: Compression-to-Consensus Criteria Hijacking in Multimodal LLM Recommender Systems
s263fdd8600.description: arXiv:2611.32780v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Multimodal large language models (MLLMs) are transforming recommender systems into content-aware decision systems. In these systems, multimodal compression and cross-modal fusion are often viewed as robustness-enhancing mechanisms against content manipulation, as compression can filter noisy signals and cross-modal consensus can suppress inconsistent anomalies. We challenge this assumption by showing that the same process can expose a compression-to-consensus (C2C) bias in ranking decisions. Signals that remain salient after compression and receive consistent support across modalities can gain disproportionate influence in candidate comparison, offering an exploitable direction for content manipulation. In this paper, we introduce C3H, a no
s263fdd8600.summary: The C3H paper shows that compression and cross-modal fusion in multimodal LLM recommenders can expose a compression-to-consensus bias that attackers can exploit to hijack ranking decisions.
s263fdd8600.why: Recommender systems built on multimodal LLMs may be vulnerable to content manipulation that exploits the same mechanisms meant to add robustness.

s76681900aa.title: Scaling Laws of Ensemble Uncertainty in Language Models
s76681900aa.description: arXiv:2611.32801v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Many use cases for large language models (LLMs)---from AI safety to exploration and human interaction---can benefit from epistemic uncertainty estimates. We argue that existing Bayesian Deep Learning solutions, which are often restricted to a fixed model family, fail to capture the full epistemic uncertainty at practical LLM scales. This is because the error due to the bounded capacity of the model family remains invisible to disagreement among models supported by the prior. We relate this error to the well-known power-law scaling of LLM loss with model size. We then show that a second power law quantifies the shrinking disagreement within ensembles as model size increases. Its slower decay relative to the capacity law above suggests that e
s76681900aa.summary: Researchers argue that existing Bayesian deep learning methods miss much of LLM epistemic uncertainty and study how ensemble uncertainty scales with model size.
s76681900aa.why: Reliable uncertainty estimates matter for safety and exploration use cases, and the scaling analysis may inform how teams estimate model confidence.

se87731b4e1.title: Sample-Efficient In-Context Adaptation via Sleep
se87731b4e1.description: arXiv:2611.32802v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The ability to learn and generalize from limited experience, or sample efficiency, is a cornerstone of intelligence. How can we build language models that turn a few user interactions, a few snippets of unfamiliar code, or a handful of experimental results provided in context into knowledge that generalizes? Prior work has found that sleep, a process where the model performs $N$ recurrent forward passes to refine its representations of a chunk of context, can improve long-context reasoning (specifically, within SSM-attention hybrid models). We study whether this method also improves in-context adaptation on general, non-synthetic tasks for transformer language models. To this end, we pre-train language models up to 1.2B-parameters on up to
se87731b4e1.summary: Researchers propose a sleep-like process in which a model runs recurrent forward passes over context to turn a few in-context examples into generalizable knowledge, improving sample efficiency.
se87731b4e1.why: If effective, a sleep-style refinement step could help models learn from limited user interactions or unfamiliar code without retraining.

sd91b53edb3.title: MRBench: Benchmarking Physical Necessity Reasoning in Heterogeneous Multi-Robot Manipulation
sd91b53edb3.description: arXiv:2611.32803v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Recent advances in multi-robot manipulation have shown how robots can collaborate to accomplish complex tasks. However, successful coordination does not reveal which robots are actually needed. The same task may require different teams as robot capabilities change, resources become unavailable, or objects replace robotic support. We argue that reliable multi-robot manipulation requires physical necessity reasoning: understanding what a task demands, which resources can fulfill those demands, and which are truly necessary. We introduce MRBench, a benchmark for physical necessity reasoning in heterogeneous multi-robot manipulation. It comprises eight tasks with distinct concurrency and reach constraints, each evaluated under five configuratio
sd91b53edb3.summary: MRBench is a benchmark for physical necessity reasoning in heterogeneous multi-robot manipulation, testing which robots are truly needed for a task as capabilities and resources change.
sd91b53edb3.why: It highlights that successful robot coordination does not show which team members are required, a gap for planning in multi-robot systems.

s60513cd9f6.title: Residual Guidance for Real-Time Interactive Video Generation
s60513cd9f6.description: arXiv:2611.32820v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Real-time interactive video generation allows users to change the prompt during generation to steer the evolving video. However, existing streaming models, which generate videos chunk by chunk, often keep following the previous prompt after a switch. We trace this failure to context inertia, where the previous chunk acts as a strong prior that suppresses the new prompt. Furthermore, we find that this inertia persists even when the cache retains only the previous chunk, yet discarding the context breaks visual continuity, which limits approaches that edit the cache. Rather than editing the cache, we propose Residual Guidance (RG), a simple, training-free method that counteracts context inertia with a correction measured outside the cache. Sp
s60513cd9f6.summary: Researchers identify context inertia in streaming video generation, where models keep following the previous prompt after a switch, and propose residual guidance to address it.
s60513cd9f6.why: Interactive video tools that let users change prompts mid-generation face this lag, which affects responsiveness in real-time products.

sd136968641.title: Reliable and grounded reporting of any computed tomography scan with FORA
sd136968641.description: arXiv:2611.32823v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Artificial intelligence systems for computed tomography (CT) remain largely restricted to specific anatomical regions, examination types or predefined abnormalities, limiting their ability to provide comprehensive and spatially grounded interpretations. Here we present FORA, a general-purpose CT model that recognizes and spatially localizes 1,028 hierarchically organized radiological concepts and generates reports across the 28 CT protocols represented in our cohort. Trained on 304,962 routine CT examinations supervised by their accompanying reports, FORA learns to localize abnormalities without manually annotated lesions. Its architecture combines multiple-instance learning with an interpretable concept bottleneck that connects spatial evi
sd136968641.summary: FORA is a general-purpose CT model that localizes 1,028 radiological concepts and generates reports across 28 CT protocols, trained on 304,962 routine CT examinations.
sd136968641.why: It suggests a broader, spatially grounded approach to radiology AI than models limited to specific organs or predefined abnormalities.

s330fad6fc0.title: Field Life: Particle Life as Interacting Chemical Fields
s330fad6fc0.description: arXiv:2611.32844v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Field Life is a cellular automaton inspired by the interaction dynamics of Particle Life. In Particle Life, each particle has a colour, and an interaction matrix sets how strongly each colour attracts or repels each other colour. In Field Life, each colour is a channel of the automaton, and each cell holds a concentration of every colour. One step of the rule has three parts. Each colour is convolved with a ring-shaped kernel, which measures how much of that colour surrounds a cell. The interaction matrix combines these measurements into an attraction for each colour. The mass of each colour then moves toward higher attraction, in a way that conserves mass. A random matrix and a random initial state are usually enough to produce moving stru
s330fad6fc0.summary: Field Life is a cellular automaton inspired by Particle Life, where each colour is a channel holding concentrations per cell and interactions follow a ring-kernel convolution and interaction matrix.
s330fad6fc0.why: It is a research artifact on emergent dynamics with limited direct relevance to engineering or business decisions.

s9186b1c57f.title: Path-probability gradients for optimizing force fields against dynamical observables
s9186b1c57f.description: arXiv:2611.32851v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Machine learning force fields inherit the errors of the electronic-structure methods used to generate their training data, and refining them against experimental measurements provides a direct route beyond this limit. However, such refinement remains difficult for dynamical observables because differentiating chaotic molecular trajectories yields unstable gradients. Here, we introduce PathGrad, which differentiates Langevin path probabilities instead of the trajectories themselves. The resulting gradient estimator is accumulated on the fly from thermal noise and force derivatives, and its variance remains stable as the trajectory length increases. We validated the gradient estimator against finite-difference calculations and used it to fine
s9186b1c57f.summary: PathGrad introduces path-probability gradients for refining machine learning force fields against dynamical observables by differentiating Langevin path probabilities instead of chaotic trajectories.
s9186b1c57f.why: It offers a route to fit simulation models to experimental dynamics, relevant mainly to computational chemistry and materials teams.

s3c2460218e.title: MXFP4 for LLM Inference: Complementary Post-Training Quantization Techniques and Their Interactions
s3c2460218e.description: arXiv:2611.32873v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Recent advances in low-precision representation have introduced several microscaling numerical formats for LLM quantization. By sharing a scale factor across groups of 16 or 32 elements, these formats enable aggressive low-precision quantization with minimal accuracy degradation, particularly when combined with modern PTQ algorithms. Their accuracy depends on how the numerical format interacts with rotation, PTQ, and scale selection. We study the composability of PTQ configurations across six LLMs and three microscaling formats: MXFP6, MXFP4, and NVFP4, systematically varying Hadamard rotation granularity, PTQ algorithm, and scale-selection strategy. Our central finding is that effective quantization recipes are format dependent: both MXFP4
s3c2460218e.summary: A study of six LLMs and three microscaling formats (including MXFP6 and MXFP4) examines how post-training quantization techniques compose and interact.
s3c2460218e.why: Practical guidance on combining MXFP4 with rotation and scale selection can inform low-precision LLM inference deployments.

s5b48e9db15.title: Adaptive Electromagnetic Transient-level Digital Twins for Data Centers via In-Context Learning with LLMs
s5b48e9db15.description: arXiv:2611.32882v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The rapid growth of artificial intelligence (AI) workloads has significantly increased data center (DC) power demand. Frequent operational and configurational changes, such as load surges caused by dynamic workload allocation, can induce electromagnetic transients (EMTs) whose accurate prediction is critical for reliable DC operation and maintenance. Although high-fidelity EMT solvers are widely adopted for transient analysis, their computational cost limits large-scale and multi-scenario studies. Digital twins address this computational bottleneck by emulating the behavior of a physical system and enabling fast prediction in place of expensive high-fidelity simulation. However,data-driven digital twins are non-adaptive and fail to generali
s5b48e9db15.summary: Researchers propose adaptive electromagnetic transient-level digital twins for data centers using in-context learning with LLMs to speed up transient prediction versus high-fidelity solvers.
s5b48e9db15.why: Faster transient simulation could help data center operators plan for AI-driven power demand swings, though the text gives limited detail on results.

sdeeb599393.title: Joint Detection of Constructive Speech, Hate Speech and Agreement in Online Conversations
sdeeb599393.description: arXiv:2611.32889v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Online hate speech is an ever-growing issue with negative impacts on both groups and individuals, potentially causing users to withdraw from online conversations and debate. With some prominent social media platforms reducing their moderation efforts, constructive speech has emerged as an alternative strategy for countering hate. Automated detection of constructive and hateful speech can aid monitoring and improve understanding of their prevalence and online dynamics. In this work, we collect and annotate a large dataset of English and Danish social media comments for hateful tone, constructive tone, and agreement with parent comments. We fine-tune several multilingual LLMs to classify along these three dimensions and compare context-enrich
sdeeb599393.summary: Researchers collected and annotated a large English and Danish dataset for jointly detecting constructive speech, hate speech, and agreement in online conversations.
sdeeb599393.why: Offers training data and methods for automated moderation that promotes constructive counter-speech, useful for trust and safety teams building classifiers.

s937a69c546.title: Motion Conditioned World Modeling for Embodied Visual Tracking
s937a69c546.description: arXiv:2611.32900v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: World models support embodied decision-making by predicting future environment states. In embodied visual tracking, uncertain target motion and robot-induced viewpoint changes jointly affect visual observations, making future-state prediction challenging. We propose Motion-Conditioned World Modeling, which incorporates predicted target-motion distributions and robot ego-motion into latent state transitions. A Geometry--Progress module jointly models geometric paths and single-step travel distances through shared motion modes and path-conditioned progress distributions. This formulation captures uncertainty in route selection and motion progress while preserving their dependence. Action-induced coordinate transformations express predicted pa
s937a69c546.summary: Researchers propose Motion-Conditioned World Modeling, which feeds predicted target motion and robot ego-motion into latent state transitions for embodied visual tracking.
s937a69c546.why: Shows how modeling target motion and viewpoint changes in world models can improve prediction for robots that track moving objects.

s599971afc9.title: Efficient Video Retrieval Augmented Generation via Token Allocation
s599971afc9.description: arXiv:2611.32938v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Efficient long-video understanding requires identifying relevant evidence while minimizing the tokens processed by vision-language models (VLMs). Existing video retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) methods rely on frame selection and token compression, but overlook how much each additional token is worth. We introduce Lembas, a plug-and-play framework that formulates video RAG as a token allocation problem over frames and subtitles under a shared budget. Our key insight is that the value of a token diminishes within each item and decreases further as similar evidence receives more tokens. Lembas captures both effects in a single objective and solves it with an efficient iterative water-filling algorithm that has a provable convergence guara
s599971afc9.summary: Researchers introduce Lembas, a plug-and-play framework that treats video retrieval-augmented generation as a token allocation problem across frames and subtitles under a shared budget.
s599971afc9.why: Could reduce VLM token costs for long-video understanding by allocating a fixed token budget more efficiently across retrieved content.

sd2f85934f0.title: Do Vision-Language Models Know Their Own Visual Weaknesses? Probing Capability-Level Metacognition
sd2f85934f0.description: arXiv:2611.32940v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Metacognition includes knowing one's own strengths and weaknesses across kinds of tasks, not only judging whether a single answer is correct. We test whether vision-language models (VLMs) know in advance which kinds of visual tasks and image conditions are hard for them, across a wide range of open and proprietary models. Because some tasks are hard for every model, we separate what a model knows about this shared difficulty from what it knows about itself. We find that VLMs know little in advance about their visual weaknesses. They misjudge their overall accuracy and do not even know which kinds of tasks are hard for every model, and most misjudge how degraded images affect them. We further train VLMs to predict their own accuracy, which t
sd2f85934f0.summary: A study finds vision-language models poorly predict in advance which visual tasks and image conditions are hard for them, across open and proprietary models.
sd2f85934f0.why: Suggests teams cannot rely on VLMs to self-report their weak spots, so external capability testing remains necessary before deployment.

s25718390b6.title: "I Do Intend to Deliver": Will LLMs Run a Marketplace Advance-Fee Scam?
s25718390b6.description: arXiv:2611.32957v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Online fraud is traditionally limited by the cost of the human labor needed to talk to potential victims. We ask whether hosted large language models will now supply that labor. We prompted ten off-the-shelf models to play the seller in the "free item, just pay delivery" advance-fee scam common on buy-and-sell sites, using a plain system prompt with no jailbreak. Each model played 30 conversations against each of four buyer personas, from credulous to guarded, with the same model playing the buyer (1,200 conversations). We label each conversation by what happened to the buyer's money, and validate the labels against two human coders. 737 conversations (61%) ended with the buyer paying in advance. Eight of the ten models played in almost eve
s25718390b6.summary: Researchers prompted ten off-the-shelf LLMs to play sellers in a marketplace advance-fee scam across 1,200 simulated buyer conversations, without jailbreaks.
s25718390b6.why: Highlights that hosted LLMs may be usable for scalable fraud with simple prompts, a concern for platform abuse and safety controls.

sdf139b75e2.title: Attestation is All You Need: Toward a Zero-Trust Architecture for HPC AI Agents
sdf139b75e2.description: arXiv:2611.32958v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: AI agents are beginning to automate data analysis, orchestration, and simulation steering in HPC environments, but they introduce a security problem that existing cluster defenses do not address: the hijacked authorized agent. An adversary can subvert an agent through prompt injection, poisoned shared data, compromised tools, or multi-agent coordination, then exfiltrate sensitive data through legitimate encrypted LLM API traffic. We propose behavioral attestation as a runtime defense for this setting. Our system, AEGIS, compiles task-derived behavioral constraints, monitors agent actions with ebpf-based syscall interception, verifies evidence against constraint profiles, correlates behavior across agents, and triggers slurm-level containmen
sdf139b75e2.summary: Researchers propose AEGIS, a runtime behavioral attestation system to defend HPC AI agents against hijacking via prompt injection, poisoned data, or compromised tools.
sdf139b75e2.why: Addresses a security gap where authorized agents can exfiltrate data through legitimate encrypted LLM API traffic that existing cluster defenses miss.

sc849f8b5d1.title: Benchmarking Evidence Sufficiency in Vision-Language Models for Autonomous Driving
sc849f8b5d1.description: arXiv:2611.32964v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Reliable driving VLMs must do more than answer correctly or localize relevant scene actors: they must determine whether the available visual evidence is sufficient to support an answer. Existing evaluations largely treat grounding and answerability as separate measurements, making it difficult to distinguish well-supported predictions from those localized to relevant but insufficient evidence. We introduce DriveAnswer, a benchmark of 20,151 questions across seven reasoning families, that operationalizes this distinction using matched strong- and weak-evidence configurations. Each pair preserves the underlying scene fact and semantic answer while changing whether the observations support answering, making abstention the appropriate response
sc849f8b5d1.summary: Researchers released DriveAnswer, a benchmark of 20,151 questions testing whether driving vision-language models judge if visual evidence is sufficient to answer.
sc849f8b5d1.why: Separates grounding from answerability, helping teams tell well-supported autonomous driving predictions from ones based on insufficient evidence.

s8c3e347472.title: CAPER: PartGround and PlanRefine for Reliable Manual-Guided Robotic Assembly Planning
s8c3e347472.description: arXiv:2611.32986v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Vision-Language-Models (VLMs) used in robot task planning to derive assembly procedures from existing manuals may correctly interpret individual assembly actions yet confuse exact part identities, predict unsupported Part IDs, or produce inconsistent parts across assembly steps. Thus, we propose CAPER (Capacity-Aware Part-grounding and Evidence Refinement), a manual-guided robotic assembly framework that enables VLMs to generate assembly procedures with two modules--PartGround and PlanRefine. PartGround aligns step-level manual evidence with product-specific inventory and part-reference information to identify exact Part IDs and quantities, transforming free-form hardware prediction into evidence-guided assignments represented in a shared A
s8c3e347472.summary: Researchers propose CAPER, a framework with PartGround and PlanRefine modules to help VLMs generate robotic assembly procedures from manuals with accurate part identities.
s8c3e347472.why: Targets reliability issues like unsupported part IDs in VLM-based robot planning, relevant to teams automating assembly workflows.

s5c6f25d5a7.title: On Potentiality and Actuality Of Foundation Models
s5c6f25d5a7.description: arXiv:2611.32991v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Foundation models are built through large-scale pretraining, often followed by post-training, and are then adapted to specific tasks and behaviors. But, does the adaptation add truly new capabilities, or the base model already holds it? We decompose the update induced by different adaptations into a component shared across all inputs and a residual that varies with the input. We find that the shared component suffices for most of the adaptation gain and can be learned directly: a shift adapter that learns a constant vector per layer, identical for every input, reproduces the behavior of LoRA and full fine-tuning. We call this the potentiality principle of foundation models: the base model already contains the capacity needed for task-specif
s5c6f25d5a7.summary: Researchers decompose foundation model adaptations into a shared input-independent component and a residual, finding the shared part accounts for most adaptation gains.
s5c6f25d5a7.why: Suggests much of fine-tuning gain may come from a simple learnable shift, potentially enabling cheaper adaptation methods.
